newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FNB Namibia lists on the Namibian exchange.
newsitem.headline: FNB Namibia lists on the Namibian exchange.

text.p: First National Bank of Namibia on Thursday became the first local bank to list on the Namibian Stock Exchange following its successful share offer.
The bank said in a statement a total of 44 million shares had been sold at 380 cents a share, totalling N$167 million. It said this represented about 22 percent of the share capital of FNB Namibia.
"The bank has operated as an autonomous company in Namibia since 1988 and it is appropriate that it has now become a Namibian listed company," FNB Namibia's managing director Stuart Moir commented.
A preferential offer of just over 1.3 million shares to the bank's employees had been 78.7 percent oversubscribed and an excess had been allocated to the public, the statement added.

It said allotments for applications of less than 250,000 shares had been granted in full for both the preferential and public offers, while applications in excess of 250,000 shares had been allocated at the discretion of the directors. Selected institutions and pension funds had fully taken up the private placement of 40.1 million shares while the public offer of 2.6 million shares was 21.2 percent oversubscribed, FNB Namibia said.
"(This) is...a tremendous vote of confidence in the bank by the Namibian public and corporates," Moir said.
